chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who became certain, after he had performed the ẓuhr prayer, that he had prayed five [rakʿahs].

He said: How did he become certain? I said: He knew. He said: If he knew that he had sat in the fourth [rakʿah], then the ẓuhr prayer is complete; so let him stand and add to the fifth rakʿah another rakʿah, and perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, and they will be counted as two rakʿahs of supererogatory prayer, and there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.جَلَسَ: sat for the tashahhud in the fourth rakʿah
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five rakʿahs instead of the prescribed number
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he becomes certain that he prayed five rakʿahs in ẓuhr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who becomes certain after ẓuhr prayer that he has prayed five rakʿahs. If he had sat in the fourth rakʿah, his obligatory prayer is valid and complete, and he should add another rakʿah to make the excess into a two-rakʿah nafilah and then perform sajdatay al-sahw.
